The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a critical parameter.

Friction force is proportional to the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a critical parameter.

Friction force is also dependent on the viscosity of the fluid surrounding the pendulum, viscosity being a critical parameter.

Viscosity of the fluid surrounding the pendulum can vary depending on the temperature and pressure, temperature being a critical parameter.

Temperature being a critical parameter, the viscous friction force should be taken into account for the physical pendulum model when the pendulum is subject to viscous damping, damping being a critical parameter.

Damping being a critical parameter, the viscous friction force should be taken into account for the physical pendulum model when the pendulum is moving at high velocities, velocities being a critical parameter.

Velocities being a critical parameter, the viscous friction force should be taken into account for the physical pendulum model when the pendulum is subject to external forces that can cause it to slow down, slow down being a critical parameter.

Slow down being a critical parameter, the viscous friction force should be taken into account for the physical pendulum model when the pendulum is in a real-world scenario, scenario being a critical parameter.
